subject: Request pile-up causing p95/p99 regressions — Acme Payments L3 escalation
messages:
From: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-payments.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden latency spike — p95 up from 180ms to ~900ms since 2am PT

Hi Dylan,

We started seeing a big jump in response times overnight for our POST /v1/generate calls — p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~900ms and p99 to multiple seconds. A few of our jobs are seeing 5xx when under load. This started around 02:00 PT and is impacting checkout flows for a small % of users (we're throttling, but still seeing customer impact).

Attached is a small sample of traces and the request ids. Can your team take a look? We are flagged as high priority on our side.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah King
Head of Platform, Acme Payments

Attachments: customer_error_logs_1105.txt (text), acme_latency_snapshot_1105.csv (csv)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-payments.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T09:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 up from 180ms to ~900ms since 2am PT

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're triaging now and I've looped Hannah (SRE) and Monica (Customer Success) to coordinate.

Immediate plan:
- We'll ingest your traces and request ids and match them to our request logs.
- SRE will look for backlog/queue depth anomalies and batching changes in the last 24 hours.
- We'll push a temporary routing change if we find a problematic pool to relieve pressure.

Can you confirm whether the affected requests are mostly the single-turn large prompt flows or many short prompts (we need to know batching behavior on your side)? Also please share any rate changes you deployed overnight.

I'll update in ~45m with our initial findings.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 up from 180ms to ~900ms since 2am PT

Quick update from SRE initial triage:
- We see a sustained increase in queue depth for the hosted-gpu pool handling Acme's tenant from ~02:00 PT onward.
- Batch sizes increased by ~2.5x for short sequences (likely due to increased concurrency + our continuous-batcher heuristics kicking in under changed traffic mix).
- There are KV cache miss rates up for certain request prefixes, leading to extra compute per request.
- No infra failures or OOMs. Error 5xxs are rate-limited worker timeouts and a few model-inference timeouts.

Tentative root cause: request pile-up + larger batching causing processing latency spike at p95/p99 rather than the typical median. The runtime's batching heuristic misestimated optimum batch boundaries under this traffic mix.

Immediate mitigations to attempt (ordered):
1) Force smaller max-batch-size for the Acme route (temporary config override).
2) Bump instance concurrency to spread batches across more workers.
3) Turn on prefix caching for their frequent prompt templates (if acceptable).
4) Fallback routing to a different instance class if backlog doesn't clear in 10 minutes.

I'll attempt (1) and (2) now and report back.

— Hannah
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-payments.com>, platform@acme-payments.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T10:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 up from 180ms to ~900ms since 2am PT

Sarah — we made two immediate changes at 10:18 PT: we reduced Acme route max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 and increased worker concurrency on the affected pool by 30%. Early indicators show p95 dropping toward normal, but p99 still elevated (we think heavy tail remains because some requests still require full model compute).

We also flagged a potential issue in our continuous-batcher heuristic where short prompt bursts are being grouped inefficiently. Marcus from runtime will be on a follow-up to propose a code-level guard.

Monica will coordinate a short maintenance window for us to flip routing to a larger instance class if we need further mitigation.

— Dylan
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 up from 180ms to ~900ms since 2am PT

Technical context from runtime team:
- The batcher uses an adaptive timeout to decide when to cut a batch. Under a sudden increase in concurrency with many short sequences, the timeout window caused batches to grow large before dispatch, increasing per-request waiting time and p95.
- We are seeing pathological cases where batch assembly waits ~60-80ms to fill a large batch; that adds directly to p95.

Short-term code-level guard I can deploy as a hotfix: cap wait-time for small-token requests at 12ms and add a per-tenant batch size multiplier override (so we can make Acme 0.25x overall batch-size).

Longer-term: smarter heuristic that factors request size distribution and prefix hotness; also prefer dynamic batching that biases low-latency SLA tenants.

I'll prepare a hotfix build and coordinate a canary push within the hour.

— Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-payments.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-11-05T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 up from 180ms to ~900ms since 2am PT

Thanks all for the fast response. We confirmed on our side that the requests that hit the checkout path are mostly short prompts (1–3 tokens returned, high QPS). We did not change traffic patterns or rates overnight intentionally — a partner push may have created short bursts.

Please keep us posted on the hotfix and any temporary limits. We'll plan to hold a short sync at 14:00 PT if useful.

-Sarah
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary and exec note — Acme p95/p99 regression (Nov 5)

Executive summary for records and Customer Service:
- Impact window: 2026-11-05T02:00:00-2026-11-05T12:40:00 PT.
- Root cause: Adaptive batching heuristic plus a traffic mix shift (burst of many short-response requests) produced larger-than-optimal batches and increased queue wait times for some requests. KV cache miss-rate amplified CPU usage for tail requests.
- Customer impact: Acme observed elevated p95 (~900ms) and intermittent 5xxs during peak backlog; internal mitigations reduced p95 toward baseline and eliminated 5xxs for the affected flows.

Actions taken:
1) Emergency mitigation at 10:18 PT: per-tenant max_batch_size override to 8 and +30% concurrency for affected pool.
2) Hotfix at 11:12 PT: runtime guard capping assembly wait-time for small-token requests to 12ms (canary->prod).
3) Short-term route failover tested during maintenance; successful with minimal client interruption.
4) Customer communication: Monica and Dylan coordinated an update to Acme and scheduled the 14:00 PT technical sync.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Engineering (runtime) to implement batching heuristic improvements and a per-tenant latency-first policy by Q1 2027.
- Product to add a per-route SLA flag so we can bias low-latency tenants into lower-batch regimes.
- CS/Account: offer Acme 1 week of complimentary credits and a joint traffic rehearsal to avoid surprises.
- Post-mortem doc and monitoring dashboards (INF-4921) updated and shared with execs.

I'll attach a short post-mortem doc and open follow-up tickets. If leadership wants a short briefing, we can prepare a 10-min slide deck.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
